title: Tech Note: Exploring 4D Ajax Framework Offline Mode
author: Thomas Fitch, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note captures a pivotal moment in web application architecture circa 2008, when browser-side offline support was still nascent and fragmented across competing technologies (emerging HTML5 vs. Google Gears). The Data Grid's Offline Mode feature allowed users to cache grid data locally, add/edit records offline, and auto-sync when reconnected—an important UX feature for mobile/remote workers before modern service workers and IndexedDB became standard. Both HTML5's Web Applications spec and Google Gears are now historical technologies (Gears discontinued 2011); modern offline-first web apps use service workers, IndexedDB, and progressive web app patterns entirely superseding this note's approach.
related_updates: HTML5 Web Applications 1.0 specification was later subsumed into the broader HTML Living Standard
Google Gears was officially discontinued in December 2011 with no successor within 4D products
4D Ajax Framework and its Data Grid component have been retired
Offline-first web application patterns today use Service Workers, IndexedDB, and PWA standards rather than browser extensions
